policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'to Pilate the governor' with no praenomen; the RP expansion adds Ποντίῳ, which ASV renders as 'Pontius' wherever it stands.
Present παραδιδοὺς and aorist παραδοὺς both come into ASV as the past 'who betrayed him'; the English aspect is not diagnostic.
ἔστρεψεν and ἀπέστρεψεν are both rendered 'brought back'; ASV wording does not separate the simplex from the compound.
The variant is the article before πρεσβυτέροις only; 'to the chief priests and elders' is compatible with either.
ASV text reads 'innocent blood' (ἀθῷον) and its textual note 'Many ancient authorities read righteous' places δίκαιον in the margin.
ὄψῃ and ὄψει are orthographic forms of the same future middle; both are 'see thou to it'.
ASV 'cast down the pieces of silver into the sanctuary' renders the goal expression εἰς τὸν ναόν, not the locative ἐν τῷ ναῷ ('in the sanctuary').
ἐστάθη and ἔστη both yield 'Jesus stood before the governor'; ASV does not distinguish the passive from the second aorist.
ASV 'And Jesus said unto him' carries an unitalicized indirect object answering αὐτῷ, which is not required by the English.
The variant is the article before πρεσβυτέρων only; 'by the chief priests and elders' fits either.
ASV names the prisoner only 'Barabbas'; the double name Ἰησοῦν Βαραββᾶν would have produced 'Jesus Barabbas'.
ASV 'Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?' excludes the prefixed Ἰησοῦν of the base, but the remaining difference is the article τὸν, which English does not show.
The variant is the article with Βαραββᾶν; the bare answer 'Barabbas' is compatible with either.
ASV 'They all say, Let him be crucified' has no indirect object; αὐτῷ would have given 'say unto him', as it does at 27:11.
ASV 'And he said' leaves the subject pronominal; the RP addition ἡγεμὼν would have been rendered 'the governor said', as in the preceding verse.
ἀπέναντι and κατέναντι are both 'before the multitude'; ASV does not distinguish them.
ASV text reads 'the blood of this righteous man', rendering τοῦ δικαίου; its note 'Some ancient authorities read of this blood' assigns the shorter base reading to the margin.
The variant is Greek word order only; 'and put on him a scarlet robe' follows English idiom and does not track either sequence. The 'clothed' note concerns the preceding participle, not this unit.
ἐπί with genitive or accusative is 'upon his head' either way; ASV does not show the case.
Within one clause ASV shifts from 'upon his head' to 'a reed in his right hand', rendering the locative ἐν τῇ δεξιᾷ rather than the directional ἐπὶ τὴν δεξιάν it had just given as 'upon'.
Aorist ἐνέπαιξαν and imperfect ἐνέπαιζον both come into the ASV chain of past narrative as 'mocked him'.
Vocative βασιλεῦ and nominative-for-vocative ὁ βασιλεύς are both 'Hail, King of the Jews!'
The variant is the position of λεγόμενος; ASV 'that is to say, The place of a skull' does not reflect Greek order.
ASV reads 'they gave him wine to drink', rendering οἶνον; ὄξος is 'vinegar' in ASV, as at 27:48.
Aorist ἠθέλησεν and imperfect ἤθελεν are both 'he would not drink'.
ASV 'if thou art the Son of God, come down from the cross' has no conjunction before the imperative, so the added καὶ is not in view.
The variant is the connective δέ, which ASV leaves unrendered often enough that 'In like manner also' settles nothing.
ASV lists only 'the scribes and elders'; the RP addition καὶ Φαρισαίων would have added 'and Pharisees'.
ASV 'He is the King of Israel' is a flat assertion; the RP εἰ would have made it conditional ('If he is the King of Israel').
πιστεύσομεν with ἐπ᾽ αὐτόν or αὐτῷ is 'believe on him' either way.
English 'deliver' requires an object, so the unitalicized 'him' in 'let him deliver him now' may be obligatory supply rather than a rendering of the added αὐτόν.
συσταυρωθέντες with or without σύν is 'crucified with him'; the compound verb alone carries the 'with'.
ἀνεβόησεν and ἐβόησεν are both 'cried with a loud voice'; ASV does not mark the preverb.
ASV transliterates the cry as 'Eli, Eli', which is Ἠλὶ ἠλί; Ἐλωῒ ἐλωΐ is transliterated 'Eloi, Eloi' in ASV at Mark 15:34.
ἑστηκότων and ἑστώτων are alternative perfect participles of the same verb; both are 'them that stood there'.
ἔλεγον and εἶπαν both appear as 'said' in ASV narrative; the aspect is not shown.
ASV ends the verse at 'to save him' and has no spear-and-water sentence, so the bracketed WH addition is absent.
The variant is the order of εἰς δύο against ἀπ᾽ ἄνωθεν ἕως κάτω; ASV's 'rent in two from the top to the bottom' is English idiom and does not fix the Greek sequence.
The variant is verb number with the neuter plural σώματα; English number follows the subject 'many bodies' either way.
γενόμενα and γινόμενα both stand behind 'the things that were done'.
The variant is the order of θεοῦ and υἱός; 'the Son of God' is the necessary English for both.
ASV reads 'Mary the mother of James and Joses'; Ἰωσῆ is 'Joses', while Ἰωσήφ would be 'Joseph', as ASV renders it in the next verse.
Passive ἐμαθητεύθη and active ἐμαθήτευσεν both yield 'was Jesus’ disciple'; ASV's stative phrasing does not choose.
ASV 'Then Pilate commanded it to be given up' resumes the body with a pronoun; an explicit τὸ σῶμα would have repeated 'the body'.
The dative σινδόνι alone is 'in a clean linen cloth' as much as ἐν σινδόνι is; the preposition leaves no English trace.
Μαριάμ and Μαρία are both 'Mary' in ASV.
ASV has 'his disciples' (αὐτοῦ, excluding the WH omission) and no 'by night', excluding the RP addition νυκτός.
The variant is the connective δέ; ASV opens 'Pilate said unto them' without one, but it drops δέ freely enough that the absence is not decisive.
